properties.description:
At 600 PM MDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm near
Rio Communities, or 5 miles east of Belen, moving northeast at 35
mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 50 mph and penny size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor damage to outdoor objects is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
Belen, Valencia, El Cerro Mission, Rio Communities North, Meadow
Lake, Tome, Rio Communities, Los Chaves and Los Trujillos-Gabaldon.

This includes Interstate 25 between Mile Markers 190 and 198.
properties.instruction:
Monitor the weather situation closely and be alert for threatening
weather conditions.

Motorists can expect brief but sudden changes in visibility and
ponding of water on roadways as storms move through the area.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 23 at 5:56PM MDT until October 23 at 9:00PM MDT by NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.description:
FFWEPZ

The National Weather Service in El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Central El Paso County in western Texas...

* Until 900 PM MDT.

* At 556 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Up to 1 inch of rain has fallen.
Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.5 inches are possible in the
warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
East El Paso, Central El Paso, Far East El Paso, Mission Valley,
Horizon City, Socorro and Sparks.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 23 at 5:44PM MDT until October 24 at 12:00AM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible although the risk will decrease into the evening as
stronger showers and thunderstorms diminish.

* WHERE...The eastern San Juan Mountains and Upper Rio Grande Valley.

* WHEN...Until midnight MDT tonight.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may exacerbate flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Waves of showers and isolated embedded thunderstorms will
continue into the evening.  Although rainfall will be more
limited in coverage, localized amounts of up to 0.5 inches could
cause additional minor rises in the smaller creeks and
tributaries.
- The eastern San Juan Mountains and Upper Rio Grande Valley with
the greatest risk across Conejos County.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible new
Flood Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be
prepared to take action should flooding develop.

properties.description:

across the warned area. Up to 0.75 inches fell in just 30 minutes
along State Road 4 and Highway 290 near Jemez Springs. Flash flooding
is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Jemez Springs, Jemez State Monument, Jemez Pueblo and Canon.

deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.description:
At 535 PM MDT, a severe thunderstorm was located 5 miles south of
Cutter, moving northeast at 30 mph.

HAZARD...Ping pong ball size hail and 60 mph wind gusts.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

damage to roofs, siding, windows, and vehicles. Expect wind
damage to roofs, siding, and trees.

Locations impacted include...
Upham, Cutter, and Spaceport America.
properties.instruction:

building.

expected.

Saturday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 8 AM Saturday to 8
PM EDT Monday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 5 PM
Saturday to 8 PM EDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur.

erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:

travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

dangerous surf conditions.

float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.
